message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look at the **federal long weekends** in Canada for 2023.  
(If you’re planning trips in a particular province, let me know – many provinces add extra holidays that also create long weekends.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if weekend) | Long‑weekend span |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Dec 30 – Jan 2** (5‑day stretch) |
| Family Day (Alberta, BC, NB, NL, PEI, SK, ON, MB) | Feb 20 (Monday) | — | **Feb 18 – Feb 20** |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | — | **Apr 7 – Apr 9** |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | — | **May 20 – May 22** |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Observed Mon Jul 3 | **Jul 1 – Jul 3** |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | — | **Sep 2 – Sep 4** |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | — | **Oct 7 – Oct 9** |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Saturday) | Observed Mon Nov 13 | **Nov 11 – Nov 13** |
| Christmas | Dec 25 (Monday) | — | **Dec 23 – Dec 25** |

> **Note:**  
> - Boxing Day (Dec 26) falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it doesn’t create a long weekend.  
> - Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., Family Day on Feb 20, or other regional holidays) that may add extra long weekends.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the provincial variations or any other details!
